messages:
Ananya: Quick sync — thinking about 'elastic slices' (sub-GPU packing) to reduce fragmentation for dedicated pools. Proposal: allow 4x slices per GPU with soft isolation; autoscaler treats slices as units for scale decisions. Thoughts?

Jorge: Interesting. How do we account for tenant QoS? slices reduce waste but increase noisy neighbor risk.

Ananya: Right. idea is soft cgroup + per-slice latency SLO. If a slice breaches SLO we throttle or promote to full GPU slot.

Evan: Could be heavy on bookkeeping. Where do we store mapping? operator vs control plane?

Ananya: Control plane stores slice metadata, operator enforces kube/node cgroups. Keep operator stateless; control plane has ledger.

infra-bot: Deploy started: canary/operator-v2 -> staging (ci-4102)

Priya: Sample config I sketched:
```
pool:
  slice_size: 0.25 # fraction of GPU
  max_slices_per_gpu: 4
  qos_slo_ms: 150
  breach_action: promote|throttle # enum
autoscaler:
  unit: slice
  scale_up_threshold: 0.8
  scale_down_threshold: 0.2
```

Jorge: How do we price slices? billing needs to reconcile fractional usage.

Ananya: Billing: charge by slice-minutes, include inefficiency tax if slice fragmentation > 20% per-pool.

Evan: Edge case: tensor-core heat/thermal slowdowns when many small slices. Can we prefer packing same-arch tenants per GPU? affinity label?

Priya: Affinity is doable. Add policy: pack_by_model_signature: true.

Ananya: Need fallback path: if operator can't create slice due to MIG limitation we fallback to single-slot allocation.

Jorge: Operationally, debugging mailbox might be messy. Need per-tenant slice traces in Console.

Priya: I'll add per-slice metrics: latency_p50/p95, GPU_util, cache_hits.

Ananya: Ok next steps: spec PR -> small simulator to measure fragmentation benefits -> billing & console hooks. Anyone want to pair on simulator?

Evan: I'll pair Wed afternoon. :+1: 

Jorge: I'll take billing integration.
